short: The inference process where a generative model samples new tokens, pixels, or audio frames conditioned on an input prompt or context.
eli5: After reading your prompt, the model writes out its answer piece by piece like an author typing live.
example: Streaming a grounded answer token by token from retrieved RAG documents.

short: Predicting a probability distribution over the entire vocabulary for which token should come immediately after the preceding sequence.
eli5: Playing fill-in-the-blank one word at a time: 'The cat sat on the ___' -> 'mat' (72%), 'sofa' (15%).
example: An LLM estimating probabilities for thousands of candidate tokens before sampling one.

short: A generative model that produces a sequence step by step, feeding each newly generated token back as context for the next step.
eli5: Writing a story where every new word you put down becomes part of the sentence you read to pick the next word.
example: Decoder-only LLMs appending each sampled token until an end-of-sequence marker appears.

short: A decoding strategy that keeps only the K highest-probability candidate tokens at each step and redistributes probability among them.
eli5: Narrowing a restaurant menu of 50,000 dishes down to only the top 40 favorites before rolling a die.
example: Using K=40 to block absurd ultra-low-probability words while keeping phrasing varied.

short: A dynamic decoding method that picks from the smallest set of top candidate tokens whose cumulative probability reaches threshold P.
eli5: Picking from a short list when one answer is super obvious, and a wider list when lots of words fit equally well.
example: Setting top-p to 0.9 so predictable facts stay crisp while open-ended metaphors stay expressive.

short: A generative architecture that learns to create crisp images or audio by reversing a gradual noise-corruption process step by step.
eli5: Starting with pure TV static and gently sculpting away the fuzz over dozens of steps until a sharp painting emerges.
example: Generating high-resolution illustrations from text prompts using latent diffusion.

short: Iteratively predicting and subtracting random Gaussian noise from a corrupted sample to recover coherent structure.
eli5: Wiping dust off a foggy window in small passes until the clear street scene shines through.
example: A U-Net or diffusion Transformer estimating noise at step t=25 out of 50.

short: A compressed internal coordinate space learned by a model where high-level attributes vary smoothly along geometric directions.
eli5: A secret control panel of hidden sliders—like 'smile amount' or 'sunset warmth'—packed inside compact numbers.
example: Interpolating halfway between two points in latent space to blend two musical styles smoothly.

short: A generative autoencoder that compresses inputs into a smooth probabilistic latent distribution and reconstructs samples back out.
eli5: A machine that shrinks a photo into a neat summary recipe and can rebuild realistic variations from nearby recipes.
example: Compressing 512x512 images into compact latent grids inside modern diffusion pipelines.

short: Two neural networks trained in competition: a Generator creating synthetic samples and a Discriminator trying to spot fakes.
eli5: An art forger and an art detective practicing against each other until the forger's paintings look indistinguishable from real ones.
example: Synthesizing photorealistic textures or upscaling blurry video frames.

short: Conditioning an image generator on natural-language text embeddings so visual synthesis matches the user's written description.
eli5: Describing a scene out loud to an illustrator—'an astronaut reading in a greenhouse'—and watching it appear.
example: Cross-attending prompt token embeddings inside a diffusion model to guide composition and style.

short: A unified AI model that natively processes and relates multiple data types such as text, images, audio, and video.
eli5: An AI that can read a paragraph, look at a diagram, and listen to a voice clip all with the same brain.
example: Uploading a whiteboard sketch and asking an assistant to turn it into working HTML and CSS.
